answer.justification: Clinical presentation of urethritis, asymmetric oligoarthritis (knee, ankle), conjunctivitis, and preceding dysentery is classic for reactive arthritis, a seronegative spondyloarthropathy. Enthesitis, especially at the Achilles tendon insertion, is a characteristic musculoskeletal feature of this condition. Other options are not typical: erythema migrans suggests Lyme disease; finger pain on passive extension is nonspecific; RLQ mass is more suggestive of Crohn's or appendicitis.
